content:
Hi,
I'm Johannes Zimmer, currently studying Math at KIT and interested in spatial stochastics and stochastic geometry and Lean 4. I would love to start contributing to Mathlib in that field.
A natural starting point would be the Fell topology, as it is later the basis for random closed sets. It was pointed out by @Attila Gáspár also in the VietorisTopology that it is not defined on closed sets (Fell would be the natural topology there).
can I just start on a fork? is there something that I should consider?

I'm not sure from your message wether your questions are technical (git stuff) or mathematical (as in, how should you developp the API). If the first, then indeed the page Filippo linked should be a good read.

More precisely about your project : Attila Gáspár is indeed the right person to talk to. I haven't followed very carefully what was happening here, but my impression is that we will not be able to avoid having various type aliases for the different topologies. We should be able to put both the vietoris and the fell topologies on both Closeds X or Set X, probably with a mechanism similar to docs#Lex or docs#WithLp. Does that make sense? @Attila Gáspár how do you feel about switching your work on the Vietoris topology from Set X to WithVietoris (Set X) / WithVietoris (Closeds X) ?

Yes I've read it.

Probably I should have been more specific. What I really wanted to ask was whether the topic is a interesting fit in general and whether there are things I should consider regarding the definitions.

In particular, I'm unsure how to set it up. I chatted/searched a bit with claude code through mathlib and found the following information: Closeds α\alphaα already carries the topology induced by the Hausdorff uniformity (from Mathlib.Topology.UniformSpace.Closeds), and the existing Vietoris file dodges the clash by putting its global instances on Compacts $\alpha$ and NonemptyCompacts α\alphaα instead, with Set α\alphaα only used as a local thing.

For Fell that does not really work as the compactness theorem (for locally compact Hausdorff base) lives on closed sets (with ∅\emptyset∅) , so I think i want Closeds α\alphaα as the carrier.

Calude code proposed doing def FellCloseds (α\alphaα) := Closeds α\alphaα and then putting the Fell topology globally on that or define it non-globally on Closeds α\alphaα and let users use it in a local instance.

As i did not want to start any work based on what an AI told me, i thought i ask a question what i should consider.

PS: don't worry i would code out everything myself once the starting point is there : ) but how to set this up is really outside of my competency area :D

As i did not want to start any work based what an AI told me, i thought i ask a question what i should consider.

Thanks, this is really appreciated.

As I wrote above, I think the thing to do is to create type aliases WithVietoris and WithFell, which do not do anything by themselves (apart from unifying the boilerplate). Then the vietoris topology should be defined on WithVietoris (Set X), WithVietoris (Closeds X), WithVietoris (Compacts X),... and the Fell topology on WithFell (Closeds X).
ok this was basically my unclarity, thanks. But that would also mean refactoring vietoris topology. So i guess the best move is to wait for an reply from @Attila Gáspár and then start working on it.
maybe the refactoring would then also be a nice small starting contribution

If you feel like starting on the refactor that would be great, but since that tends to be quite a painful task I wouldn't necessarily recommend it as a first project. Maybe you can setup the type alias for what you're really interested about (the Fell topology), and doing so first will teach you what needs to be done in the refactor ?

I'm not sure that we need a WithVietoris alias. First of all, if we have the Hausdorff metric on Compacts and NonemptyCompacts, then we automatically have the Vietoris topology on them. I don't know any other reasonable topology that coincides with the Vietoris topology in the metric case, so it probably makes sense to have it as an instance on Compacts and NonemptyCompacts.

Alternatively, we could make the Hausdorff metric instances on Compacts and NonemptyCompacts scoped instances or add a WithHausdorff alias. However, NonemptyCompacts has had the Hausdorff metric since its introduction in 2019 (see mathlib3#696). In fact, it looks like the entire reason for introducing NonemptyCompacts was to have a type where the Hausdorff distance is a (finite) metric. This instance is also used in the GromovHausdorff file, so it may not be easy to do this change.

For Compacts, I made the Hausdorff metric an instance a few months ago, so it's unlikely to break anything if we make the instance scoped (or add a type alias). But I think it's good to have consistency between Compacts and NonemptyCompacts (the reason Compacts didn't have a metric for a long time is that it was actually introduced later than NonemptyCompacts).

On Set, there is no topology defined as an instance, so it is enough to just make the Vietoris topology a local instance wherever it is needed. Also, I expect that most uses of the Vietoris topology would be for Closeds or (Nonempty)Compacts. So the only case where WithVietoris could be useful is Closeds, which has the Hausdorff metric (also introduced in mathlib3#696). However, there are currently no results about Closeds. Despite the comment in the VietorisTopology file that these could be added in the future, I have no plans to do this.

For the Fell topology, the WithFell type alias makes more sense, since it's different from the Vietoris topology even for Compacts over a metric space. But if it will only be used on Closeds, then it's probably simpler to just have a FellCloseds type alias. On Set, it may even be a disadvantage to use a type alias because it may make it more difficult to state relations between the different topologies (e.g. vietoris ≤ fell over a T2 space).

Johannes Zimmer said:

For Fell that does not really work as the compactness theorem (for locally compact Hausdorff base) lives on closed sets (with ∅\emptyset∅) , so I think i want Closeds α\alphaα as the carrier.

I haven't checked all the details, but I think you could prove the compactness for Set α, then transfer this result to FellCloseds α similarly to how it's done for the Vietoris topology.
Ok thanks, for all the information! i will start working on Fell and post here once i have further questions or something to show. thanks a lot.
